user.title: Find your battery
user.description: Look up your battery in the [BatteryLedger Store]({store_url}): {count} batteries, list dated {updated}. Or enter its details yourself.

store_search.title: Search the BatteryLedger Store
store_search.description: Filter the {count} batteries in the Store. Leave any filter empty to include everything.

data_description.region: Warranty terms often differ by country, so pick the one where the battery is installed.

store_select.title: Choose your battery modules
store_select.description: {matches} matching batteries (✓ = checked by a maintainer). Tick **every** model installed in this system, e.g. both BAT 8.0 and BAT 10.0 if you have a mix. You'll enter how many of each, and when their warranty started, next.

manual.title: Enter battery details
manual.description: Use the figures from your manufacturer's datasheet and warranty for your country. Enter throughput in kWh (23.77 MWh = 23770 kWh).

data.reported_kwh: Capacity reported by the inverter per unit (kWh)

data_description.regions: Comma-separated country codes, e.g. AU, NZ.
data_description.throughput_table: Only for 'Table by unit count': one row per line as units=kWh, e.g. 3=60000.
data_description.series: Product line, e.g. SigenStor or Neo.
data_description.model: The battery module or unit as the manufacturer names it, e.g. SigenStor BAT 8.0.

group.title: {name}

data_description.install_date: The date picker shows dates in the format set in your Home Assistant user profile (Profile → Date format).

add_more.title: Battery groups

menu_options.store_search: Add another model or later install from the Store

system.title: System and costs

data_description.cost: What you paid for the batteries, for cost per kWh and remaining value. Leave empty to skip the cost sensors.
data_description.reported_capacity_entity: The battery capacity your inverter reports, used to check the configured units match the hardware.
data_description.soh_entity: The health % your inverter reports, compared against the warranty floor.
data_description.currency_style: Symbol: {symbol} and {symbol}/kWh, as in the original YAML package. Code: {currency} and {currency}/kWh, shown as money in each user's own currency format.
